name: Darjeeling
description: Darjeeling is a hill station in the lower Himalayas at around 2,000 m, known for its tea gardens, views of Kangchenjunga, and the colonial-era toy train. It suits travellers who enjoy cool mountain air, walking, and a slower pace, but the crowded main town, frequent fog, and monsoon disruptions can test patience. Best visited between mid-March to May and October to November.

attractions.name: Tiger Hill
attractions.description: A viewpoint at 2,590 m where visitors gather before dawn to watch the sunrise turn Kangchenjunga and, on very clear days, Everest golden. The view is spectacular when conditions cooperate, but fog or cloud cover — common even in peak season — can blank the entire horizon.

attractions.name: Darjeeling Himalayan Railway (Toy Train)
attractions.description: A UNESCO World Heritage narrow-gauge steam railway running since 1881, offering a slow, scenic ride through tea estates and hill towns. The joy ride section between Darjeeling and Ghum is the most popular option and takes about an hour each way; the full Darjeeling–NJP run takes most of a day and is often delayed.

attractions.name: Happy Valley Tea Estate
attractions.description: One of Darjeeling's oldest working tea gardens, open to visitors for guided walks through the plucking rows and a look at the processing factory. The estate is at its most interesting during the first and second flush seasons (March–April and May–June); outside flush the factory may be closed.

attractions.name: Batasia Loop
attractions.description: A spiral railway loop engineered to lose altitude quickly, surrounded by a garden and a war memorial. The toy train passes through the loop in a scenic spiral, and the viewpoint gives open panoramas of Darjeeling town and the mountains behind it on a clear day.

attractions.name: Yiga Choeling Monastery (Ghoom)
attractions.description: Founded in 1850, this is one of the oldest Tibetan Buddhist monasteries in the Darjeeling hills and houses a large Maitreya Buddha statue. The atmosphere is genuinely contemplative and the resident monks are accustomed to respectful visitors; it is also conveniently close to the Ghoom toy-train station.

attractions.name: Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoological Park
attractions.description: A high-altitude zoo at around 2,134 m that is one of the few places in India where you can see snow leopards, red pandas, and Himalayan wolves in an accredited conservation setting. Enclosures are spacious by Indian zoo standards, but the walking circuit is hilly and can be tiring for elderly visitors.

attractions.name: Himalayan Mountaineering Institute (HMI)
attractions.description: Founded in 1954 after Tenzing Norgay's first ascent of Everest, this institute houses a museum with genuine expedition artifacts, early climbing gear, and exhibits on Himalayan geography. It sits inside the zoo campus so the two are typically combined in one visit.

attractions.name: Sandakphu Trek
attractions.description: At 3,636 m, Sandakphu is the highest point in West Bengal and offers one of the finest Himalayan panoramas in India — four of the world's five tallest peaks visible on a clear day. The standard 5–6 day return trek from Maneybhanjang is strenuous with significant altitude gain; a Land Rover option exists but the track is rough.

attractions.name: Mirik Lake (Sumendu Lake)
attractions.description: A small man-made lake in the hill town of Mirik, popular for boating and walks along a pine-lined promenade. The setting is pretty and relatively uncrowded compared to Darjeeling town, and the surrounding area has cardamom gardens and orange orchards worth a short wander.

attractions.name: Tinchuley Village
attractions.description: A quiet Lepcha–Nepali eco-village about 28 km from Darjeeling town, largely unknown to mass tourism, offering sweeping views of Kangchenjunga, orange and cardamom farms, and genuine homestay accommodation. Roads are narrow and the last stretch is steep; it is best treated as an overnight detour rather than a day trip.
